Inherited from Prakrit 𑀘𑀫𑀓𑁆𑀓 (camakka). Cognate with Punjabi ਚੌਂਕਣਾ (cauṅkṇā). Related to चमकना (camaknā, “shine”) and चमचमाना (camacmānā, “sparkle”).

Derived from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀘𑀉𑀓𑁆𑀓𑀝𑁆𑀞𑀻 (caükkaṭṭhī, “doorframe”) or a related term (with possible metathesis of the aspiration), from Sanskrit *चतुष्काष्ठ (*catuṣkāṣṭha, “rectangular frame”), from चतुर् (catur, “four”) + काष्ठ (kāṣṭha, “wood, timber”). Compare Gujarati ચોકઠું (cokṭhũ), Marathi चौकट (caukaṭ), Punjabi ਚੁਗਾਠ (cugāṭh) / چُگاٹھ (cugāṭh), ਚੌਖਟ (caukhaṭ) / چَوکھٹ (caukhṭ), ਚੌਖਟਾ (caukhṭā) / چَوکھٹا (caukhṭā), Nepali चौखुट (caukhuṭ), Maithili चौकठि (caukᵊṭhɨ) / 𑒔𑒾𑒏𑒜𑒱 (caukaḍhi), Odia ଚୌକାଠ (caukāṭha), Bengali চৌকাঠ (cōukaṭh), Assamese চৌকাঠ (soukath).
